extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners (and patent practitioners reviewing examiner practice)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for preparing and applying rejections under 35 U.S.C. 102 (anticipation/prior art) and 35 U.S.C. 103 (obviousness), including provisional rejections, priority/benefit date determinations, and related procedural requirements for U.S. patent examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: International application as 35 U.S.C. 102(e) prior art (conditions)
rubrics_metrics.description: To rely on an international filing date for prior art purposes under 35 U.S.C. 102(e), the international application must have been filed on or after November 29, 2000, must have designated the U.S., and the international publication by WIPO under PCT Article 21(2) must have been in English.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If any one of the conditions is not met, the international filing date is not a U.S. filing date for prior art purposes under 35 U.S.C. 102(e). If not met, the international publication may instead be applied under 35 U.S.C. 102(a) or (b) as of its publication date. See form paragraphs 7.08 and 7.09.

rubrics_metrics.name: International publication not in English or not designating U.S. (effect on 102(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: If an international application was published by WIPO in a language other than English, or did not designate the U.S., the WIPO publication, the U.S. publication of the national stage application, and a U.S. patent issued from the national stage may not be applied as a reference under 35 U.S.C. 102(e).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such references may be applied under 35 U.S.C. 102(a) or (b) as of their publication date. See form paragraphs 7.08 and 7.09 for handling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-AIPA treatment for international applications filed before Nov 29, 2000
rubrics_metrics.description: If the reference is a U.S. patent resulting directly or indirectly from an international application filed prior to November 29, 2000, the prior art date of the reference is determined under pre-AIPA 35 U.S.C. 102(e).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use form paragraph 7.12.01 in this situation; do not apply post-AIPA 102(e) amendments. Caution that WIPO publication might still have an earlier prior art date under 102(a) or (b).

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of priority/benefit claims for determining 102(e) date
rubrics_metrics.description: In determining the 35 U.S.C. 102(e) date, consider priority/benefit claims to earlier-filed U.S. provisional applications (35 U.S.C. 119(e)), U.S. nonprovisional applications (35 U.S.C. 120 or 121), and international applications (35 U.S.C. 120, 121 or 365(c)) only if the subject matter used to make the rejection is appropriately supported in the relied‑upon earlier‑filed application's disclosure (and any intermediate application(s)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A benefit claim to a U.S. patent of an earlier-filed international application may only result in an effective U.S. filing date as of the date the requirements of 35 U.S.C. 371(c)(1),(2) and (4) were fulfilled. Do NOT consider benefit/priority to U.S. applications filed before an international application, nor foreign priority claims under 35 U.S.C. 119(a)-(d) and 365(a).

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph sequencing requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain MPEP form paragraphs (e.g., 7.12, 7.12.01, 7.13, 7.14, 7.15 family) must be preceded by form paragraph 7.07 and may be preceded by one or more of form paragraphs 7.08 to 7.11, or alternately by form paragraph 7.103 as specified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure required preceding paragraphs are included when using a form paragraph; the manual repeatedly warns which paragraphs must precede others (e.g., 7.12.01, 7.13, 7.14, 7.15 variants).

rubrics_metrics.name: 35 U.S.C. 102(f) (applicant not the inventor) rejection criterion
rubrics_metrics.description: A claim may be rejected under 35 U.S.C. 102(f) where the applicant 'did not himself invent the subject matter sought to be patented.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include an explanation of the supporting evidence establishing that applicant was not the inventor (see MPEP § 2137). This form paragraph must be preceded by form paragraph 7.07 and may be preceded by 7.08–7.12.

rubrics_metrics.name: 35 U.S.C. 102(g) (priority of invention) criterion
rubrics_metrics.description: Under 35 U.S.C. 102(g) priority is determined by considering dates of conception and reduction to practice and the reasonable diligence of one who was first to conceive and last to reduce to practice, to a time prior to conception by the other; also consider whether another made the invention in this country without abandonment, suppression, or concealment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this standard when priority disputes arise (e.g., interferences). This form paragraph must be preceded by form paragraph 7.07 and may be preceded by one or more of 7.08–7.13.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rejection wording for 35 U.S.C. 102(a)/(b)/(g)
rubrics_metrics.description: Form paragraph 7.15 wording: 'Claim [1] rejected under 35 U.S.C. 102[2] as being [3] by [4].' In bracket 3 insert either '--clearly anticipated--' or '--anticipated--' with an explanation; in bracket 4 insert the prior art relied upon.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This rejection must be preceded by appropriate form paragraphs (7.07 and others) or form paragraph 7.103, and must be followed by either form paragraph 7.15.02 or 7.15.03 when 102(e) is also being applied. Provide explanatory material when using 'anticipated' vs 'clearly anticipated.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Provisional rejection under 35 U.S.C. 102(e) (common assignee or inventor)
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim provisionally rejected under 35 U.S.C. 102(e) as being anticipated by a copending application with a common assignee or at least one common inventor; based on presumption of future publication or patenting of the copending application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This provisional rejection may be overcome by (a) a showing under 37 CFR 1.132 that any invention disclosed but not claimed in the copending application was derived from the inventor of the instant application, or (b) an appropriate showing under 37 CFR 1.131. It may not be overcome by filing a terminal disclaimer. Use form paragraph 7.15.01 with explanatory text in bracket 4 as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rejection under 35 U.S.C. 102(e) (common assignee or inventor) — use and limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Use 7.15.02 to reject when the applied reference has a common assignee or common inventor and, based upon earlier effective U.S. filing date of the reference, it constitutes prior art under 35 U.S.C. 102(e).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The rejection may be overcome by derivation/declaration under 37 CFR 1.132 or showing under 37 CFR 1.131. Apply the amended 35 U.S.C. 102(e) (AIPA/2002) when appropriate (e.g., filed under 111(a) or WIPO publication meeting the Nov 29, 2000 conditions). For international-app-derived references with filing dates prior to Nov 29, 2000, apply pre-AIPA 102(e) (form paragraph 7.12.01).

rubrics_metrics.name: Rejection under 35 U.S.C. 102(e) (no common assignee/inventor)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use 7.15.03 when rejecting over a patent or patent application publication with an earlier filing date that discloses but does not claim the same invention, where the reference need not have a common assignee or inventor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply AIPA/amended 102(e) as appropriate; if the reference is a U.S. patent issued from an international application filed prior to Nov 29, 2000, use pre-AIPA 102(e). Patent application publications may be used only if preceded by form paragraph 7.12.

rubrics_metrics.name: 35 U.S.C. 102(b) public use or on-sale rejection content
rubrics_metrics.description: When rejecting under 35 U.S.C. 102(b) based upon a public use or sale of the invention, the examiner must insert a full explanation of the evidence establishing the public use or sale.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This form paragraph must be preceded by form paragraphs 7.07 and 7.09 or by 7.103. Provide detailed factual support in bracketed explanation.

rubrics_metrics.name: 35 U.S.C. 102(c) abandonment rejection content
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim rejected under 35 U.S.C. 102(c) because the invention has been abandoned; examiner must insert a full explanation of the evidence establishing abandonment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP § 2134 for further guidance. Precede with required form paragraphs (7.07/7.09 or 7.103).

rubrics_metrics.name: 35 U.S.C. 102(d) foreign patenting rejection content
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim rejected under 35 U.S.C. 102(d) as being barred by foreign patenting; the rejection must include appropriate dates and explanation of how they make the foreign patent available under 102(d).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Precede with required form paragraphs (7.07 and 7.11 or 7.103) and refer to MPEP § 2135 for applicable 35 U.S.C. 102(d) prior art.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contents required in a 35 U.S.C. 103 rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: After indicating the rejection under 35 U.S.C. 103, the examiner should set forth: (A) relevant teachings of the prior art relied upon (with references to columns/pages/lines), (B) the differences in the claim over the applied reference(s), (C) the proposed modification of the applied reference(s) necessary to arrive at the claimed subject matter, and (D) an explanation why one of ordinary skill in the art at the time would have been motivated to make the proposed modification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These elements are required to communicate the basis for the rejection and to establish a prima facie case of obviousness. Cite specific locations in references when appropriate. This form paragraph must be preceded by form paragraph 7.07 and 7.10 or by 7.103.

rubrics_metrics.name: Three basic criteria for prima facie obviousness
rubrics_metrics.description: To establish a prima facie case of obviousness: (1) there must be some suggestion or motivation to modify the reference or to combine reference teachings; (2) there must be a reasonable expectation of success; (3) the prior art reference(s) must teach or suggest all the claim limitations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The teaching/suggestion and the reasonable expectation of success must be found in the prior art and not based on applicant’s disclosure. See MPEP §§ 2143–2143.03 and decisions such as In re Vaeck for pertinent authorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner's burden to present convincing line of reasoning
rubrics_metrics.description: The initial burden is on the examiner to provide some suggestion of the desirability of doing what the inventor has done; either the references must expressly or impliedly suggest the claimed invention or the examiner must present a convincing line of reasoning why the artisan would have found the claimed invention obvious in light of the references.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Ex parte Clapp and MPEP § 2144–2144.09 for examples of reasoning supporting obviousness rejections. Provide a clear, reasoned rationale rather than mere conclusory statements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of all relied references in rejection statement
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a reference is relied on to support a rejection, whether or not in a minor capacity, that reference should be positively included in the statement of the rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See In re Hoch: ensure every cited reference appears in the written rejection so the record is complete and transparent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Importance of clear written record for rejections
rubrics_metrics.description: It is important for an examiner to properly communicate the basis for a rejection so that issues can be identified early and applicant can have a fair opportunity to reply; the written record must clearly explain the rationale for decisions during prosecution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because examiners cannot normally be compelled to testify regarding mental processes, the written record must clearly explain rationale; this is especially important because issued patents are presumed valid (35 U.S.C. 282). See MPEP § 2141–2144.09 for guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provisional rejection (obviousness) disqualification under 35 U.S.C. 103(c)
rubrics_metrics.description: Subject matter that was prior art under former 35 U.S.C. 103 via 102(e) is disqualified as prior art against the claimed invention if the prior art and the claimed invention were, at the time the invention was made, owned by the same person or subject to an obligation of assignment to the same person; CREATE Act adds joint research agreement disqualification subject to three conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CREATE Act conditions for joint research agreement disqualification: (A) the claimed invention was made by or on behalf of parties to a joint research agreement in effect on or before the date the invention was made; (B) the invention was made as a result of activities within the scope of the joint research agreement; (C) the patent application discloses or is amended to disclose the names of the parties to the joint research agreement. These changes apply to patents granted on or after Dec 10, 2004 (and to pending applications as specified). See MPEP § 706.02(k) and § 706.02(l)(1).

rubrics_metrics.name: When to make provisional rejection for copending applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Where two applications of different inventive entities are copending, not published under 35 U.S.C. 122(b), and the filing dates differ, a provisional rejection under 35 U.S.C. 102(e)/103 should be made in the later filed application unless excluded under 35 U.S.C. 103(c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The confidential status of unpublished applications must be maintained. The provisional rejection alerts applicant that an actual rejection may follow if one application issues, giving applicant opportunity to act to avoid loss of rights. See MPEP § 706.02(k) and § 706.02(f).

rubrics_metrics.name: Ways to overcome a provisional 35 U.S.C. 102(e)/103 rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: A provisional rejection of the obviousness type under 35 U.S.C. 102(e)/103 can be overcome by: (A) arguing patentability over the earlier filed application; (B) combining subject matter into a single application claiming benefit under 35 U.S.C. 120 and abandoning copending applications (subject to 35 U.S.C. 112 support requirements); (C) filing an affidavit/declaration under 37 CFR 1.132 showing derivation; (D) filing under 37 CFR 1.131 showing date of invention prior to the effective U.S. filing date of the copending application; (E) for applications pending on or after Dec 10, 2004, showing common ownership or disqualification under CREATE Act joint research agreement conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note that combining applications and obtaining 120 benefit requires earlier applications to provide adequate 35 U.S.C. 112 support for the claims in the later application. Terminal disclaimers and 1.130 affidavits/1.321(c) may be used in certain common ownership situations to overcome double patenting/103 rejections. See MPEP §§ 715, 718 and relevant form paragraphs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of restriction/continuation practice on provisional rejections
rubrics_metrics.description: If a provisional rejection is made and the copending applications are combined into a single application and the resulting single application is subject to a restriction requirement, the divisional application would not be subject to a provisional or actual rejection under 35 U.S.C. 102(e)/103 because 35 U.S.C. 121 precludes the use of a patent issuing therefrom as a reference against the other application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Resulting continued prosecution and continuation-in-part benefit issues are discussed; use examples (MPEP examples 1–5) to illustrate outcomes. Ensure correct application of 35 U.S.C. 121 and continuation practice.
